It raises weight, reps, or sets over time based on your logged data, so you get overload without planning it.

## Where Fitbod falls short (the honest limits)

### Weight suggestions need calibration.

Early on it can throw out odd numbers - reviewers report suggestions like 35 lb lateral raises or absurd shrug loads. It learns as you correct it, but the first few sessions are rough.

### No real injury filter.

If you tweak a shoulder, there's no clean way to exclude all overhead pressing - you manually skip or swap. Frustrating for anyone managing chronic pain or recovery.

### The free "trial" is three workouts.

After that it locks. Fitbod is effectively a paid app; the free tier isn't a sustainable option.

# Fitbod App Review 2026: Cost, AI Workouts & Results

Amanda Roberts

Amanda Roberts|Jun 13, 2025

Fitbod App Review 2026: Cost, AI Workouts & Results

Fitbod's real value is that it removes the decision-making from strength training - open the app, and it hands you a workout built around what you trained last, what you recovered, and what equipment you have. That's genuinely useful if you like lifting but hate programming. What most reviews overstate is the "AI": Fitbod plans a workout before you start, it doesn't adapt set-by-set while you train. Knowing that distinction is the difference between the right expectation and a disappointed one. [...] ### Can Fitbod handle injuries?

Not well. There's no injury filter, so you manually skip or swap exercises you can't do. That's its most requested missing feature.

### What's better than Fitbod?

Depends on your goal: StrongLifts or JEFIT for powerlifting-style programming, Freeletics for bodyweight, MyFitnessPal for nutrition. Fitbod wins for adaptive strength programming.

### Is Fitbod beginner friendly?

Yes - it handles the planning, demos every exercise on video, and ramps difficulty gradually, so beginners aren't left guessing what to do or how much to lift.

### How does Fitbod track progress?

It logs sets, reps, weight, total volume, and streaks, and uses a muscle-recovery map to shape future sessions. Treat its calorie-burn estimates as a guide, not an exact figure.

results.title: Expert-Tested: Fitbod Review (2026) | Garage Gym Reviews
results.content:
As someone who trains specifically for his sport, Caine wanted to see whether the AI-generated workouts were well-devised (and effective). He also was eager to find out how easily you could customize your plans, as not everyone has a goal of snatching 400 pounds (props to him, though!).

Overall, Caine found Fitbod to be extremely user-friendly, which is one of the key factors that determines whether you’ll keep using an app or just let it take up precious space on your phone. However, as all of our expert product testers do, he pointed out a few shortcomings that may affect your decision to roll with Fitbod.

To paint a fair and balanced picture of what the app can and can’t do, I’ll break down each category Caine assessed and provide some extra commentary of my own. [...] Obviously, the majority of users aren’t training to compete in Olympic lifting, so this may not be a dealbreaker for you.

“The other training methodologies seemed reasonable, so I’m only taking off 1 point here,” Caine says.

## Accountability

Product Rating – 4

Average Workout App Rating – 3

One of the biggest advantages of working with a certified personal trainer is that you have an actual human who can get in your ear (even remotely) and motivate you to stick to your plan. Obviously, that’s not the case with Fitbod, which relies on AI rather than a real-life coach.

Still, not all hope is lost in terms of accountability. In fact, Caine still gave a very respectable 4-out-of-5 rating here. [...] Workout apps typically do a good job of providing clear, detailed descriptions of each exercise, and many also include high-quality video demos that allow you to see how a movement should be executed.

Thankfully, Fitbod checks both of those boxes.

Images from the Fitbod app show instructions on how to perform a technique

Images from the Fitbod app show detailed instructions and videos from multiple angles to demonstrate how to perform a technique

“There are great videos and instructions for each exercise,” Caine says.

There is a caveat, though, that forced us to stick with a solid-but-unspectacular score of 3 out of 5.

“The programs that the app makes only guess at weights, so you end up guessing the stimulus, percentages, and purpose of each part of the workout,” Caine explains.
